newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher on CPI hopes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher on CPI hopes.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed higher on Thursday on hopes for a relatively low October consumer price index (CPI), to be released on Friday, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.68 percent, or 1.32 points, to 195.37 on all-share turnover of 71 million shekels against 51 million on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.57 percent to 204.91.

"Investors believe that the Bank of Israel will lower short-term rates by 0.5 percentage point following the release of October's CPI which is expected to be around 0.8-0.9 percent," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House.
"Despite the low volume the market rose during the last week. The deal on Hebron seems imminent and the market is ready for another rise," Weisberg added.
U.S. officials said on Thursday that an Israeli-Palestinian deal on partial Israeli troop withdrawal from the West Bank city of Hebron looked to be about a week away.
IDB Holding Corp rose 3.25 percent to 1,202. Traders could not explain the rise.
Clal Electronics Industries gained 3.0 percent to 24,572 after its subsidiary Scitex Corp, traded on Nasdaq, surged 17.6 percent on Wednesday.

Nice Systems gained 2.0 percent to 7,034 after Salomon Brothers reiterated its strong buy recommendation for the company. Nice reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings of $0.22 a share. Salomon estimates the company will earn $0.74 a share in all of 1996 and $1.24 in 1997 against $0.06 in 1995.
Agan Chemical Manufacturers rose 1.25 percent to 5,524 after reporting a rise in third-quarter net profit to 12.9 million shekels from 8.9 million shekels a year earlier.
Shekem surged 9.5 percent to 98.5 and traders said it was a technical correction following a sharp decline of more than 50 percent since the beginning of the year.
Africa Israel Hotels Resorts rose 5.75 percent to 309. On Wednesday Africa jumped 9.0 percent and traders said there were rumours about a purchase offer for the company's shares.

"The market is waiting for the release of the CPI figure, which is expected to be around 0.6-0.7 percent. The Bank of Israel will have to cut the rates because of the slowing economy and the declining money supply," said Ronen Kaufman at Y.L.R. Capital Markets.
"The market is waiting for a deal over Hebron. This together with the fact that bond yields fell sharply during the last few weeks is very good for the market," Kaufman said.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 0.5 percent to 149,544 on volume of 5.1 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which fell 1.0 percent to 449 on volume of 4.0 million shekels; and Discount Investments, which gained 0.25 percent to 20,368 on volume of 2.7 million shekels.
